On Mon, Apr 27, 2026 at 09:26 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Anita's note and traces.

Quick triage summary from infra:
- Observed: a sustained increase in queue depth across the regional pool servicing us-east-1 between 08:02–09:10 PST; average GPU util rose from 62% -> 92% in the affected host set.
- Root cause likely multi-factor: a short-lived hot-tenant burst from a non-reserved tenant (auto-burst policy allowed spill) plus an unexpected slow-down in KV-cache hit rate for Riverside's prefix (cache invalidation around 07:58 due to a metadata refresh).
- Impact: requests stayed in the runtime queue longer; autoscaler attempted to spin additional workers but provisioning lag (kernel warm-up + slot binding) caused transient 503s when queue hit configured tail SLO thresholds.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (ordered):
1) Reroute Riverside's reserved traffic to a nearby underutilized reserved pool (can be done in ~6–8 min).
2) Temporarily enable a prioritized prefix cache pin for Riverside to restore warm-hit rate (~3 min).
3) If accepted, issue a one-time burst credit authorization to allow overflow into dedicated burst pool for 30 min while we stabilize.

I'll start 1) and 2) now; implementing 3) needs Marissa/finance sign-off. I'll post logs and a short runbook link when done.

— David

Hi Anita — quick update and what we completed: 

What we did (completed):
- Rerouted Riverside's reserved traffic to an alternate reserved pool in us-east-1 (completed at 10:12 PST).
- Applied a short-lived prefix-cache pin to restore hit rate (applied at 10:15 PST).
- Issued a one-time burst credit authorization for 30 minutes (approved internally; spent: $1,050) while the reroute converged.

Observed results: queue depth returned to baseline within ~9 minutes after reroute; 5xx occurrences dropped to near-zero. We continue to monitor the settlement window for the rest of today and will run an extended cache warmup test tomorrow morning.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering will provide a root-cause ticket by EOD (we will include kernel/kv-cache artifacts).
- We propose a 48h postmortem and a timeline for a persistent mitigation (pin + soft isolation for high-frequency settlement prefixes) — expect the postmortem by April 29 COB.
- If you prefer, we can schedule an immediate 30-minute call to walk through traces and the temporary mitigations.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the settlement window is critical. We're treating this as Priority P1 for the next 48 hours.

Best,
